newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana govt may earn more from central bank.
newsitem.headline: Botswana govt may earn more from central bank.

text.p: A new Bank of Botswana Act, gazetted last week, could lift government earnings from its central bank significantly, bank governor Quill Hermans said on Wednesday.

Windfall central bank profits are already set to deliver the Botswana government its 14th budget surplus in 1996/97, despite initial projections of a deficit. Central bank receipts are set to reach 1.5 billion pula ($5.5 billion) from 1.05 billion in 1995/96.
But those sums, which reflect both the pula's devaluation and a sharp jump in reserves to 17.9 billion pula, could gain more under the new rules set out by the Act.
"There will be a potentially larger sum of money available for distribution to the goverment," Hermans said.
Until now, the government has received 95 percent of the bank's net income plus 10 percent of the balance standing in a foreign reserve revaluation account.
That revaluation reserve -- which held windfall gains, or unforseen losses, as the result of changes in the value of the pula -- has now been scrapped.

As a result, forex-based gains or losses on the reserves will go straight into either the bank's general reserve or the profit and loss account. Since the government will still get 95 percent of the bank's net income, it will potentially have access to a far greater percentage of any forex-based gains.
Hermans said the revaluation account had become excessive.

"The account rose to a level way in excess of what anyone could reasonably expect to be a revaluation loss. In August, we would have had to appreciate the pula by 30 to 40 percent to wipe it out," he said.
-- Barry Baxter, Gaborone newsroom +267 347182 ($ = 0.273 Botswana Pula)
